input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers two administrator-facing reports in the RHOAI web console:
a per-project idle-workbench report and a stale pipeline-run report, each
exportable as CSV. Both reports are read-only views over data that already
exists in the platform — the notebook controller's activity tracking and
Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata — so no changes are made to those components;
the console work is purely surfacing the data.

## Scope

- Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console showing, for each
  workbench, its last activity, owner, and reserved resources, sourced from
  the notebook controller's activity tracking.
- Stale pipeline-run report in the web console showing completed pipeline
  runs older than a configurable age that have retained artifacts, sourced
  from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- The configurable age threshold for the stale pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report, available to administrators, containing the
  same rows and columns as the on-screen report.
- Read-only reporting only — automated reclamation/deletion of idle resources
  and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing last-activity times,
  the console displays a per-project report listing each workbench's last
  activity, owner, and reserved resources, and the values reconcile with the
  notebook controller's activity-tracking data (passive-component validation).
- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of differing ages, the
  console displays a report listing the completed runs older than the
  configured age along with their retained artifacts, and the values
  reconcile with Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata (passive-component
  validation).
- The age threshold for the stale pipeline-run report is configurable and the
  report reflects changes to it.
- An administrator can export either report as CSV, and the CSV contains the
  same rows and columns as the on-screen report.
- No code changes are required in the notebook controller or Kubeflow
  Pipelines; both are consumed strictly as existing data sources.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from notebook-controller activity tracking.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of either report. Bundled because the
  export renders the same report surfaces HLR-1 and HLR-2 build — it shares
  their rows and columns and has no standalone surface, so it is not
  separately schedulable as its own epic.

# Documentation for the idle and stale resource reports

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the RHOAI web console's
idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run reports: what each report shows, where
the data comes from, how the stale-run age threshold is configured, and the
safe steps administrators can take to reclaim capacity based on the reports.

## Scope

Content outline (topics authored in the RHOAI documentation set):

- A doc topic explaining the per-project idle-workbench report: its columns
  (last activity, owner, reserved resources), its source (notebook controller
  activity tracking), and how to read it.
- A doc topic explaining the stale pipeline-run report: its columns, the
  configurable age threshold and how to change it, its source (Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata), and how retained artifacts are indicated.
- A doc topic covering CSV export of either report.
- A doc topic covering safe reclamation steps an administrator can take for
  resources identified as idle or stale — manual, administrator-driven steps
  only. Automated reclamation/deletion and cost/chargeback calculations are
  out of scope per the strategy and must not be documented as features.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports, including every column each
  report displays, the data source behind each, and the CSV export action.
- Published documentation explains how to configure the stale-run age
  threshold.
- Published documentation describes safe, manual reclamation steps consistent
  with the strategy's out-of-scope boundaries (no automated reclamation, no
  cost/chargeback).
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented console
  reports so that documented columns, configuration, and behavior match what
  shipped.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016 (Idle resource reporting in the web console)

## Triage Outcome

Strategy proceeded to full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only).
Rationale: although the code scope is small and confined to one active
component, the strategy spans two distinct work streams — console code
implementation (HLR-1/2/3) and substantive documentation authoring (HLR-4, new
doc topics explaining the reports and safe reclamation steps) — which warrant
separate PR review cycles. The affected-components list also spans three
components (web console, notebook controller, Kubeflow Pipelines), two of which
are passive data sources.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Documentation for the idle and stale resource reports | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9016-E001: Idle and stale resource reports in console]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9016-E002: Documentation for the reports]
    E001 --> E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation describes the reports that the console implementation delivers; it must be written against what was actually built. Per the docs-authoring priority exception, E002 inherits P2 from the strategy's `priority: Normal` frontmatter rather than pushing priority upstream. |

No other edges: E001 is the only code Implementation epic (single component,
single team, one logical change — two report surfaces in the same console with
the same work-product type), so there is nothing to parallelize or serialize
against it. No Investigation epics exist (see below).

## Component Mapping

Strategy component names mapped to canonical RHAI Jira components
(`.context/rhai-components.txt`):

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Classification |
|--------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | Active — code changes (both reports, CSV export) |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Passive — existing activity-tracking data source; no code changes |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Passive — existing run-metadata data source; no code changes |

All three components exist in `.context/architecture-context/`
(`dashboard.md`, `notebooks.md`, `data-science-pipelines.md`), so no new
component was detected and no onboarding chain (repo/license/Konflux) is
needed. The Dashboard is already Konflux-onboarded per its context file, and no
`konflux-onboarding` epic exists in this decomposition.

Passive components: the same consuming team (RHOAI Dashboard) validates both
data sources, so per Step 2 no separate validation epics are generated —
validation is folded into E001's acceptance criteria (report values must
reconcile with the notebook controller's activity tracking and Kubeflow
Pipelines run metadata).

## Investigation Epics

None. The strategy's Open Questions section is explicitly "None", and there
are no risks, assumptions-with-conditions, pending reviews, or conditional
ADRs. The strategy's premise — "the notebook controller already tracks
last-activity timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion
metadata — the data exists" — is corroborated by architecture context
(`notebooks.md`: last activity tracked per kernel; `data-science-pipelines.md`:
KFP v2 REST API with runs surfaced in the Dashboard). Which exact API surface
the console reads the activity timestamps from is API-surface discovery, an
implementation detail for the Dashboard team (captured as an acceptance
criterion on E001), not a genuine unknown that changes which epics exist.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic |
|-----|----------|------|
| HLR-1 (idle-workbench report) | P1 | E001 |
| HLR-2 (stale pipeline-run report) | P1 | E001 |
| HLR-3 (CSV export) | P2 | E001 (bundled) — CSV export renders the same report surfaces HLR-1/HLR-2 build; it shares the reports' rows and columns and has no standalone surface, so a split would touch the same UI twice and is not separately schedulable |
| HLR-4 (documentation) | P2 | E002 |

HLR-1 and HLR-2 are kept in one epic: same component (Dashboard), same team
(RHOAI Dashboard), same work-product type (console code), and both reports are
presentations over per-project resource data the console already surfaces —
they are one logical change (an administrator reporting section), not
architecturally distinct sub-systems. They are both P1, so no priority split
applies. HLR-3 (P2) is bundled per the rationale in the matrix row above.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking)**: the strategy has no Impacted
  Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria,
  and no Non-Functional Requirements section. Owner teams were inferred from
  architecture context (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard; Documentation → RHOAI
  Documentation). Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs rather
  than strategy-level ACs.
- **Scope trap watch (non-blocking)**: the stale-run report's "retained
  artifacts" column implies artifact storage metadata is reachable from run

  team should degrade gracefully rather than expanding scope into storage

  reclamation — support keeping out).
- No priority inversions detected: the only cross-epic priority difference
  (E001 P1 → E002 P2) is the intended docs-authoring exception, and E002 does
  not block any P0/P1 work.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable. There are no external dependencies with uncertain timing; all
data sources are in-platform and GA per architecture context.
